question: What fish sampling context does Jumawan et al. (2016) report for Marikina River, and can its species label, aggregate sample count, or related reproductive publications be treated as independent site-level presence evidence?

source.citation: Jumawan, J. C., Herrera, A. A., Jumawan, J. H., & Vallejo, B. M., Jr. (2016). Size structure and reproductive phenology of the suckermouth sailfin catfish Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus (Weber 1991) from Marikina River, Philippines. ARPN Journal of Agricultural and Biological Science, 11(1), January 2016.
source.accessMethod: The publisher-linked PDF and issue listing were located. This review used the publisher-PDF text returned by indexed search, including the article title, abstract, methods, results, Figure 1 station labels and copyright line. The issue-page fetch returned a Unicode decoding error in the review tool; no access control was bypassed and no PDF, figure or map was retained.
source.copyrightAndReuse: The PDF prints ©2006-2016 Asian Research Publishing Network (ARPN), All rights reserved. No item-specific open license or separate reuse grant was identified. This review records bibliographic and methodological facts only; it does not redistribute article text, tables, figures, map, specimen images or measurements.

studyDesign.gearAsReported: Cast net, 5 m long with 3.8 cm mesh
studyDesign.localityInterpretation: The methods prose explicitly names San Jose/Rodriguez/Rizal and Banaba/San Mateo. Figure 1 labels five study stations: San Jose, Banaba, Tumana, Malanday and River Park. The figure was not digitized; no coordinates, reach geometry or site-to-administrative-boundary polygon was transcribed. The named stations span the shared Marikina River research context, but no individual fish count is assigned to a station.

reportedHostFishCounts.meaning: The paper reports 607 females and 526 males caught over the 12-month study. These are host-fish samples used for size and reproductive analyses; they are not population abundance, fishery landings, catch-per-unit-effort, or a complete river inventory.

studyDesign.stationCountAllocation: No station-by-taxon or station-by-sex count table was found in the reviewed text. Do not divide or allocate the aggregate 1,133 fish among the five stations.
studyDesign.voucherAndSequenceStatus: No voucher catalogue numbers or sequence accessions surfaced in the reviewed article text. This is not evidence that specimens or supporting records do not exist elsewhere.
studyDesign.samplingLimit: The study is a historical, targeted host-fish research sample; it does not measure current presence, abundance or the full fish community at each locality.

identityAndPublicationLineage.sourceLabelDecision: Preserve Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus as the name reported by the 2016 article, not as an independently verified specimen identification or canonical species assertion.
identityAndPublicationLineage.barcodeCaveat: The related 2011 Marikina DNA-barcode review reports 36 Pterygoplichthys specimens from five named stations and finds that COI, morphology and database matches do not consistently resolve P. pardalis, P. disjunctivus and intermediate patterns. The 2016 article cites possible introgressive hybridization. This identity uncertainty is relevant, but the 36 barcode fish are not shown to be the same individuals as the 1,133 host-fish sample.

relatedReproductivePublications.citation: Jumawan, J. C., & Herrera, A. A. (2014). Ovary morphology and reproductive features of the female suckermouth sailfin catfish, Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus (Weber 1991) from Marikina River, Philippines. Asian Fisheries Science, 27, 75-89. https://doi.org/10.33997/J.AFS.2014.27.1.006
relatedReproductivePublications.relationship: The full 2014 paper reports 607 females from the same five Marikina River stations, July 2010-June 2011 period, and identical 5 m/3.8 cm cast-net specification as the 2016 paper. The 2016 paper also explicitly cites Jumawan and Herrera (2014) histological analyses for its 499-female GSI subset. This is a high-confidence cohort-level match, although no individual fish identifiers are given.
relatedReproductivePublications.decision: Count the 2014 paper’s 607 females as the female component of the 2016 sample, not a second 607-fish cohort. Preserve exact individual overlap as unverified and do not allocate fish to individual stations.

relatedReproductivePublications.citation: Jumawan, J. C., & Herrera, A. A. (2015). Histological and ultrastructural characteristics of the testis of the invasive suckermouth sailfin catfish Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus (Siluriformes: Loricariidae) from Marikina River, Philippines. Tissue and Cell, 47(1), 17-26. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tice.2014.10.005
relatedReproductivePublications.relationship: The indexed abstract describes the 2010-2011 reproductive season and the 2016 article cites this earlier male-gonad work. It is related research from the same annual period; individual specimen overlap and data lineage were not established here. Do not count it as an independent field survey.

identityAndPublicationLineage.independenceDecision: The 2014 ovary-morphology article and 2016 life-history paper share a high-confidence female cohort: both report the same 607 females, 2010-2011 period, five stations, and gear, and the 2016 paper explicitly references the 2014 histology. Count the females once; individual specimen identity is not proven. The 2015 male-reproductive paper covers the same annual period but has no specimen-level crosswalk and is not counted as an independent survey. The 2011 barcode series is separate unless a specimen crosswalk appears.

femaleCohortCrosswalk2014To2016.matchingEvidence: Same 607 females; same July 2010-June 2011 period; same five named stations; same 5 m cast net and 3.8 cm mesh; 2016 paper cites the 2014 histological analysis for its 499-female GSI subset.
femaleCohortCrosswalk2014To2016.decision: High-confidence shared female cohort; count 607 once in the 2016 total of 1,133. No individual specimen ID crosswalk is documented.

evidenceDecision.decision: Retain this paper as a historical, source-reported Marikina River host-fish study with a five-station research context and an aggregate sample total. Do not promote its P. disjunctivus label to a verified species record or allocate sample counts to NCR, Rizal, or individual stations.

nonClaims: The 1,133 fish are not an abundance estimate, fishery catch, catch-per-unit-effort, or complete fish inventory.
No count is assigned to San Jose, Banaba, Tumana, Malanday, River Park, Rizal, or NCR individually.
The source-reported Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus label is not resolved by the 2011 barcode study and is not independently re-identified in this review.
The 2014 and 2015 reproductive publications are not counted as independent survey confirmations; exact specimen overlap is unknown.
The article does not establish current presence, present abundance, native or invasive status, fishing access, legal catchability, fish safety, or a natural-diet recommendation.
No map-derived coordinates, station polygons, river geometry, or species image are created from Figure 1.
nextActions: Keep the Marikina River record in research-only status while continuing NCR and CALABARZON source discovery across freshwater, brackish and marine habitats.
Only revisit the source-reported species label if a specimen-linked voucher or independent diagnostic evidence can be tied to this 2010-2011 sample.
Do not create site counts or coordinate geometry unless a source provides a verifiable station-to-specimen crosswalk and reuse terms are reviewed.
